statement: A record's source names where a claim came from; a record's lifecycle names what standing it has earned. A presentation that groups by source alone, where the grouping implies standing, silently promotes anything from an authoritative source regardless of its actual status.
classification: Structural invariant (candidate causal pattern). Governs any surface that renders material by category where the category reads as an authority claim.

occurrences.defect: The prompt's 'constitutional constraints (non-negotiable)' section originally selected members by provenance alone: `i.provenance === 'constitutional-substrate'`. But provenance is a SOURCE claim (which pass retrieved this) and the section's heading is a STANDING claim (this bounds what may be built). A constitutional-substrate invariant sitting at status 'proposed' — a hypothesis about constitutional matters, not yet ratified — would have been rendered under 'non-negotiable' purely because of where it came from. Fixed by requiring mayBeCitedAsEstablished(lifecycle) in addition to the provenance check; a proposed constitutional member now falls through to the candidate-and-risk-signals section, where its own marker already states what it is.

canaries.assertion: 'a PROPOSED constitutional member is a signal, not a constraint' — a constitutional-substrate invariant at status 'proposed' is asserted to land in candidate-and-risk-signals, never in constitutional-constraints, at any budget.

notes: WHY THIS IS EASY TO WRITE WRONGLY. The word 'constitutional' itself sounds like an authority claim, so a filter that keys on 'is this from the constitutional substrate' feels like it is already keying on standing. It is not — the substrate holds proposed hypotheses about constitutional matters as well as canonical ones (see types/invariants.ts InvariantStatus), and only status distinguishes them.

STATED CAUSALLY: the condition is that a presentation's grouping matches the AXIS its heading claims to represent. 'Group by source, but the heading claims standing' is the specific instance found; the general condition — presenting by one axis under a heading that names a different axis — is the hypothesis, untested beyond this one occurrence.

ONE OCCURRENCE, RECORDED HONESTLY. Whether this recurs in other surfaces that group by source (e.g. a receipts drawer grouping by receipt TYPE under a heading implying VERIFIED) is unexamined. No sweep has been run; none is claimed.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE ENVELOPE CONTRACT (types/invariantEnvelope.ts). The envelope already keeps provenance and lifecycle as two required, independent fields for exactly this reason — this occurrence is a case where a CONSUMER of that contract still managed to conflate the two axes at the point of composition, showing that a correct contract does not by itself prevent a composer from ignoring half of it.
